key_insight: The paper extends the $J$-integral to 3D quasicontinuum fracture simulations and adds uncertainty quantification so crack-driving force estimates are both multiscale-consistent and statistically defensible.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable fracture assessment in large-scale atomistic-to-continuum models, including practical silicon crack-growth simulations with atomistic resolution near the crack tip.
method: Implemented $J$-integral evaluation in QC3D using Cauchy-Born-derived continuum fields under plane strain.
Validated against LEFM and virtual crack extension across linear elasticity, nonlinear Cauchy-Born, and atomistically relaxed cases.
Used Markov chain Monte Carlo to quantify uncertainty from mesh and integration-domain choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with LEFM and VCE across all three regimes, and the silicon three-point bending prediction closely matches the Griffith criterion.
watch_item: Results depend on mesh resolution, integration domain selection, and the plane-strain/QC3D assumptions, so careful calibration is needed for other geometries or material systems.
paper_title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
